profile.intro: I'm Chanthorn, a software engineer with 7+ years of experience building enterprise applications, solving technical challenges, and guiding development teams.
about: Over the past 7+ years I've worked across backend and frontend engineering, mostly on enterprise applications such as insurance, distribution, auction, and CRM systems.

Alongside hands-on development, I've led frontend and project teams — mentoring developers, reviewing code, and working with clients and stakeholders to turn business requirements into working software.
I care most about software that is reliable and maintainable: clear data models, careful handling of transactions and concurrency, and code that the next developer can understand.

projects.title: Real-Time Auction & E-Commerce Platform
projects.summary: Developed and maintained a real-time auction and e-commerce platform using Java Spring Boot and Vue.js, supporting live bidding, concurrent transactions, and online shopping workflows.
projects.overview: An auction and e-commerce platform where many users can bid on the same item at the same time and see new bids as they happen. It includes customer-facing auction and shop interfaces and an admin dashboard.
projects.challenge: Concurrent bids on the same item must be accepted or rejected safely so the recorded winning bid stays consistent, while every watching user sees the change in real time.
projects.myRole: Project Leader / Team Lead with hands-on development across the Java Spring Boot backend and the Vue.js frontend.
projects.team: Built collaboratively with my development team. Alongside my own backend and frontend work, I led the team through code reviews, mentoring, and day-to-day technical coordination with developers. Integrations not listed under my contributions were delivered as a team effort.
contributions: Java Spring Boot backend development.
Vue.js frontend development for auction participation and e-commerce.
Real-time auction features.
Redis distributed locking for concurrent bidding.
Transactional bidding workflows to keep bid data consistent.
MySQL query and backend API optimization.
projects.approach: Standard business operations go through REST APIs on a Java Spring Boot backend. Bids for the same item are serialized with a Redis distributed lock, and each accepted bid is written to MySQL through MyBatis inside a transaction so the stored result stays consistent. Accepted bids are pushed to connected clients over WebSocket. RabbitMQ handles asynchronous event processing outside the request flow, and OneSignal delivers push notifications to users. Vue.js powers the auction and e-commerce interfaces and the admin dashboard.
projects.lessons: Concurrency issues need to be designed for explicitly — locking and transaction boundaries are part of the business logic, not an afterthought.

projects.title: YesCAR — Customer Relationship Management System
projects.summary: Developed and maintained a CRM platform that digitized customer management, sales leads, and reporting. Contributed to backend and frontend development, resolved a production N+1 query performance issue, and implemented large-volume data exports.
projects.overview: The YesCAR CRM platform replaced manual paperwork with digital workflows for managing customer information, sales leads, customer relationships, and sales reports.
projects.challenge:
After deployment to production, growing customer data exposed an N+1 query problem in an existing customer phone number update workflow. The original implementation fetched records, evaluated matching conditions in application memory, and performed repeated database operations, creating a performance bottleneck. Non-unique customer names and phone numbers also complicated identifying the intended records without changing unrelated ones.

Exporting thousands of CRM records for reporting and business operations was a second engineering challenge.
projects.myRole: As a Senior Java Developer, I worked on Java Spring Boot backend services, Spring Data JPA persistence, Vue.js frontend features, and REST API integration. I also investigated and resolved the production N+1 query issue and implemented large-volume CRM data exports.
projects.team: The CRM was developed collaboratively by a development team. The customer phone number update feature had been implemented before I took ownership of its performance issue. I investigated and optimized that workflow while contributing to backend, frontend, and export functionality.
contributions: Developed backend services using Java and Spring Boot.
Used Spring Data JPA for database access and persistence.
Developed Vue.js frontend functionality and integrated REST APIs.
Supported customer, lead, and sales reporting workflows.
Investigated a production N+1 query problem in an existing customer update feature.
Identified inefficient application-level record fetching and repeated database operations.
Replaced the affected workflow with direct conditional database updates.
Eliminated unnecessary in-memory record checking and the N+1 query pattern.
Implemented data exports involving thousands of CRM records.
Supported troubleshooting and maintenance.
projects.approach:
The CRM uses Java Spring Boot backend services with Spring Data JPA for data access, exposing REST APIs consumed by a Vue.js frontend.

Set-based update optimization: I investigated the production bottleneck and replaced the application-level processing with direct conditional database updates. The database now evaluates the matching conditions and updates the intended records itself, which eliminated the N+1 query pattern in the affected workflow, avoided loading records into application memory, and removed unnecessary database round trips. Because customer names and phone numbers are not unique, the update conditions still had to be defined carefully to target only the intended records. The result resolved a production performance bottleneck and improved the efficiency and scalability of customer information updates.

Large-volume export: I implemented CRM data export functionality capable of handling thousands of records to support business reporting and operational needs.
projects.lessons: Performance problems in enterprise applications may only become visible under real production data volumes. ORM query behavior and application-level record processing need careful attention, especially with growing datasets and non-unique customer information. Direct database operations can significantly simplify inefficient workflows.
